The fed funds rate is about 0.40%, which fits the period after the December 2015 hike. The unemployment rate is 4.9%, and the 10-year yield is 1.56%. Core CPI is 2.3% and headline CPI is 1.09%. Both fit late 2016 or early 2016.

The 12-month change in the 10-year yield is -0.5pp. The 10-year was about 2.2% in Nov 2015 and about 1.56% in Nov 2016 would be -0.6pp, but the level fits other months better. In Oct 2016 the 10-year was about 1.8%, so 1.56% is lower than that. In Sept 2016 it was 1.6%, and the fed funds rate was 0.40% in Sep and Oct 2016. Headline CPI was 1.5% in Sep 2016, which is too high. Headline CPI of 1.09% fits Feb–Apr 2016 better (0.9–1.1%), but the 10-year was about 1.8% then.

Checking July 2016: the 10-year was about 1.46%, fed funds 0.39%, unemployment 4.9%, and headline CPI 0.8%. Payrolls over the 3 months were strong, with June at 290k, so the average was about 230k. The 3-month change of +114k also fits, because April–May were weak. The data point to June 2016, when the 10-year was about 1.49%; July's 3-month average was about 230k. Equity 1m return of 0.0% fits June 2016 (+0.3%) or August 2016 (+0.1%). August 2016: the 10-year was 1.56%, unemployment 4.9%, fed funds 0.40%, headline CPI 1.06%, and payrolls averaged about 230k over June–August (292, 252, 151, averaging about 232). That matches August 2016.
